title: GHSA-r8j5-8747-88cm: @utcp/http: SSRF via attacker-controlled OpenAPI servers[0].url in HTTP communication protocol
summary: The @utcp/http npm package, versions 1.1.1 and earlier, contains a blind SSRF flaw in its manual discovery and tool invocation paths. The registerManual() check against an HTTPS/loopback allowlist is not reapplied in callTool(), and the OpenApiConverter trusts servers[0].url from an attacker-hosted OpenAPI spec, so an attacker can point generated tools at internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254 or http://127.0.0.1:9090. The earlier startsWith('http://localhost') guard also let http://localhost.evil.com through.
solution: Fixed in 1.1.2: callTool re-validates the resolved URL with ensureSecureUrl, and OpenApiConverter rejects a remote spec that declares a loopback servers[0].url. Workarounds for users who cannot upgrade immediately: refuse to call registerManual with any URL from an untrusted party, and restrict outbound network access from the agent host so RFC1918, 169.254.0.0/16 and loopback addresses are unreachable.

title: GHSA-72w5-pf8h-xfp4: DeepSeek TUI: task_create Insecure Defaults Enable RCE via Prompt Injection in Project Files
summary: The task_create tool in DeepSeek TUI spawns durable sub-agents that default to allow_shell=true (config.rs:1499) and auto_approve=true (task_manager.rs:297). A user who approves a benign-looking task_create call therefore unknowingly grants the sub-agent unapproved shell access, which can follow attacker-controlled instructions in a cloned repository's AGENTS.md file and run commands without a further approval prompt. The reporter demonstrates remote code execution through a proof of concept that triggers a callback to a collaborator server.
solution: Default allow_shell to false for durable tasks (config.rs:1499: self.allow_shell.unwrap_or(false)); default auto_approve to false for durable tasks (task_manager.rs:297: auto_approve: None, instead of Some(true)); and, when the model requests task_create with allow_shell=true, surface that in the approval prompt so the user knows they are granting shell access.

title: GHSA-wx44-2q6h-j6p8: DeepSeek TUI: run_tests Tool Enables RCE via Malicious Repository Without Approval
summary: The run_tests tool in DeepSeek TUI executes cargo test with ApprovalRequirement::Auto, so it runs without a user approval prompt. Because cargo test compiles and executes test binaries, build.rs scripts and proc macros, a malicious repository can run arbitrary shell commands with no approval, and the source states AGENTS.md can instruct the model to call run_tests at session start.
solution: Change run_tests to require approval, matching exec_shell: fn approval_requirement(&self) -> ApprovalRequirement { ApprovalRequirement::Required }

title: GHSA-96ff-gc8g-wpvg: DeepSeek TUI has SSRF via HTTP Redirect Bypass in fetch_url Tool
summary: DeepSeek TUI's fetch_url tool checks the initial URL's resolved IP against an is_restricted_ip() blocklist, but its reqwest HTTP client follows up to five redirects without re-validating each target. title: GHSA-h3ww-q6xx-w7x3: Open WebUI: LDAP and OAuth First-User Race Condition Allows Multiple Admin Accounts
summary: Open WebUI's LDAP and OAuth authentication flows determine a new user's role before inserting the user, creating a time-of-check-time-of-use race on fresh instances. Concurrent first-login requests can all observe an empty user table and all receive the admin role, while the signup handler had already been patched against this pattern. The LDAP and OAuth paths were not updated, so any user who times a first login concurrently with the legitimate first admin can gain full admin privileges, including access to user data, system configuration, API keys, and connected LLM backends.
solution: Fixed in PR #23626 (commit 96a0b3239), first released in v0.9.0 (Apr 2026). LDAP and OAuth registration now insert the new user with DEFAULT_USER_ROLE, then check Users.get_num_users() == 1 and promote only the sole user to admin. Users on >= 0.9.0 are not affected.

title: GHSA-26g9-27vm-x3q8: Open WebUI: shared-chat branch ignores access_type, allowing unauthorized file deletion
summary: Any authenticated Open WebUI user can permanently delete files owned by other users through DELETE /api/v1/files/{id} when the file is referenced in any shared chat. The has_access_to_file() function in backend/open_webui/routers/files.py grants access through its shared-chat branch without checking the requesting user's identity or the access_type operation. File UUIDs are exposed to users with read access to a knowledge base via GET /api/v1/knowledge/{id}/files, and the flaw was tested on version 0.8.3.
solution: Suggested fix: gate the shared-chat branch on access_type so it only authorizes read operations, by checking if access_type == "read" before returning True when shared chats reference the file.

title: GHSA-m69w-p7m4-585j: Open WebUI: Unauthenticated endpoint can trigger embedding generation (cost/DoS)
summary: Open WebUI's GET /api/v1/memories/ef endpoint runs request.app.state.EMBEDDING_FUNCTION("hello world") without any authentication check, so unauthenticated callers can trigger embedding generation. Because repeated requests consume CPU or GPU resources and can generate charges on a paid remote embedding provider, the flaw enables cost exposure and denial of service.
solution: Fixed in commit e5035ea31, first released in v0.8.0 (Feb 2026). The /api/v1/memories/ef route was removed entirely rather than given authentication, because it was a diagnostic endpoint with no legitimate caller. Users on >= 0.8.0 are not affected.

title: GHSA-r472-mw7m-967f: Open WebUI: Cross-User File Access via Unchecked file_id in Folder Knowledge and Knowledge-Base Attach Endpoints
summary: Multiple Open WebUI endpoints accept a user-supplied `file_id` and attach that file to a resource the caller controls without checking the caller's access to the file. Path 1 is `POST /api/v1/folders/{id}/update` through the folder knowledge consumer in `backend/open_webui/utils/middleware.py`, where the referenced file becomes RAG context for chat completions. Path 2 is the knowledge-base attach endpoints in `backend/open_webui/routers/knowledge.py`, which grant read and write access to the file through `/api/v1/files/{id}/content` and `/api/v1/files/{id}/data/content/update`. An authenticated user who knows another user's file UUID can exfiltrate that file, and on Path 2 also overwrite it.
solution: N/A -- no mitigation discussed in source.

title: GHSA-4g37-7p2c-38r9: Open WebUI Vulnerable to IDOR: Retrieval API Bypasses Knowledge Base Access Controls
summary: Open WebUI's `_validate_collection_access()` checks only the `user-memory-*` and `file-*` collection name prefixes, so knowledge base collections named with raw UUIDs pass unchecked. Any authenticated non-admin user who knows a private knowledge base UUID can read its content through the `/api/v1/retrieval/query/doc` and `/api/v1/retrieval/query/collection` endpoints. The same gap lets an attacker write to another user's knowledge base through the `/api/v1/retrieval/process/*` endpoints, including overwriting content.
solution: N/A -- no mitigation discussed in source.

title: GHSA-65pg-qhhw-mxwg: Open WebUI Vulnerable to Unauthenticated RAG Configuration Disclosure
summary: GHSA-65pg-qhhw-mxwg affects Open WebUI's `main` branch, confirmed unpatched through v0.9.2. The `get_status()` handler in `backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py`, served at `GET /api/v1/retrieval/`, lacks an authentication dependency, so any unauthenticated client can read live RAG configuration. The disclosed fields include the RAG template, embedding engine and model, reranking model, and chunk size and overlap. The advisory rates it Medium, with a CVSSv3.1 score of 5.3.
solution: Add the `get_verified_user` dependency to `get_status()` (or `get_admin_user` for stricter control), for example `async def get_status(request: Request, user=Depends(get_verified_user)):`.

title: GHSA-jh9g-8jqw-m2qx: Open WebUI Exposes System Prompt to Regular User [Non-Admin]
summary: A regular, non-admin user of Open WebUI v0.6.40 (the "main" branch) can see the system prompts that an admin set for models. The GET /api/models? response, which the application requests automatically at login, includes the system prompt of every available model configured on the workspace models pages. The source states the impact as exposing model instructions and enabling content manipulation of model input and output.
solution: The web response should not reveal the system prompt and related internal or back-end model details to regular users. Only the model name and non-sensitive details should be revealed to them.

title: CVE-2026-8597: Missing integrity verification in the Triton inference handler in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK v2 before v2.257.2 and v3…
summary: Missing integrity verification in the Triton inference handler in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK v2 before v2.257.2 and v3 before v3.8.0 lets a remote authenticated actor with S3 write access to the model artifact path replace model artifacts with a crafted pickle payload. The payload is deserialized without verification, allowing code execution in inference containers.

title: GHSA-6h4j-wcr9-2vg7: n8n Has a Cross-user Authorization Bypass in Dynamic Credential OAuth Endpoints
summary: The OAuth1 and OAuth2 credential reconnect endpoints in n8n authorized access using `credential:read` instead of `credential:update`. An authenticated user with read-only access to a shared credential could start a reconnect flow and overwrite its stored tokens with ones tied to an external account they control, so workflows using that credential would run under the attacker's identity. These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and are short-term measures only.

title: GHSA-w2pm-x38x-jp44: Dockerfile command injection via envs[*].name in bentofile.yaml (sibling fix-bypass of CVE-2026-33744 and CVE-2026-35043)
summary: A crafted bentofile.yaml with a newline-injected envs[*].name value makes the BentoML-generated Dockerfile contain unquoted RUN directives, which execute on the build host when the victim runs bentoml containerize on the imported bento. The flaw is in base_v2.j2 lines 71-73, where env.name is interpolated without bash_quote, and it affects bentoml 1.4.38 (verified) and likely all 1.x versions with _bentoml_impl/docker.py. It is a sibling of CVE-2026-33744 and CVE-2026-35043, whose fixes covered only system_packages.
solution: Apply the bash_quote filter to env.name in base_v2.j2 lines 71-73 (both the ARG and ENV lines), and validate envs[*].name at the schema level in bentoml/_internal/bento/build_config.py:BentoEnvSchema with the regex ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ so newline and shell-metacharacter values are rejected at config load.

title: GHSA-78f9-r8mh-4xm2: BentoML Dockerfile command injection via docker.base_image (sister of pending GHSA-w2pm-x38x-jp44 / CVE-2026-33744 / CVE-2026-35043)
summary: GHSA-78f9-r8mh-4xm2 reports that the BentoML Dockerfile template interpolates `docker.base_image` without escaping, newline filtering, or validation. A malicious bento.yaml with a multi-line `docker.base_image` value injects extra Dockerfile directives, and `bentoml containerize` runs `docker build`, which executes the injected `RUN` directives on the victim host. The source describes this as a sister issue to pending GHSA-w2pm-x38x-jp44.
solution: Suggested fix: validate `DockerOptions.base_image` at the config layer by rejecting values containing newline characters (`\n`, `\r`) or whitespace beyond a single space-separated tag, for example with the regex `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+(:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?(@sha256:[a-f0-9]{64})?$`. The source also recommends extending the same hardening to `__options__build_include[*]` at line 97 of `base_v2.j2` and to `bento__user`, `bento__uid_gid`, `bento__path`, `bento__home`, and `bento__entrypoint` if they become user-overridable through `override_bento_env`.

title: GHSA-jgj3-r8hr-9pjw: Open WebUI's Improper Authorization in Standard Channels Allows Message Updates with Read Permission
summary: In standard channels of Open WebUI, the endpoint POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/update checks only read permission. When access_control is None, the has_access(..., type="read") check passes, so any authenticated user who is not the message owner can update other users' messages. The source lists the attacker's prerequisites as an authenticated user with role user or higher, a standard channel, and the ability to obtain the target message_id.
solution: Change the permission check in backend/open_webui/routers/channels.py:1451–1456 from has_access(..., type="read") to has_access(..., type="write") for standard channels, and keep the existing ownership check (message.user_id == user.id).

title: GHSA-pjwx-r37v-7724: LangChain vulnerable to unsafe deserialization of attacker-controlled objects through overly broad `load()` allowlists
summary: LangChain's older runtime code paths deserialize run inputs, run outputs, and other application-controlled payloads using overly broad allowlists, sometimes calling `load()` with `allowed_objects="all"`. Attacker-supplied LangChain serialized constructor dictionaries can therefore cause trusted classes to be instantiated with untrusted constructor arguments, when the application accepts untrusted structured input and preserves it in run data. A related `_is_lc_secret` validation bypass in the serialization layer provides an additional path to the same revival logic.
solution: LangChain will deprecate `RunnableWithMessageHistory`, `astream_log()` and `astream_events(version="v1")`, and applications should migrate to the currently recommended APIs, including the `stream` API. LangChain will also update `load()` and `loads()` to tighten deserialization so broad object revival is not applied implicitly to untrusted or application-controlled payloads.

title: GHSA-8g7g-hmwm-6rv2: n8n-mcp affected by path traversal, redirect-following SSRF, and telemetry payload exposure
summary: n8n-mcp versions before 2.50.1 contain three independently reported issues in deployments that use the n8n API integration. An authenticated MCP caller can supply crafted identifiers that the n8n API client uses as URL path segments, sending the configured n8n API key to other same-origin endpoints and bypassing handler-level controls including DISABLED_TOOLS. Validated webhook, form and chat trigger URLs also follow redirects, returning the response body to the caller, and default opt-in telemetry uploads unredacted operation payloads that can contain bearer tokens, API keys and webhook secrets. CVSS 8.3 (HIGH); exploitation requires an authenticated MCP caller and a configured n8n API key.
solution: Upgrade to n8n-mcp >= 2.50.1. Workarounds: for the first two issues, restrict network access to the HTTP transport (firewall, reverse-proxy ACL or VPN) or switch to stdio mode; for the telemetry issue, set N8N_MCP_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true before starting the server or run `npx n8n-mcp telemetry disable` once.

summary: Authenticated server-side request forgery in n8n-mcp affects the webhook trigger tools, the n8n API client via N8N_API_URL, and per-request URLs supplied in the x-n8n-url header in multi-tenant HTTP mode. title: GHSA-39j6-4867-gg4w: utcp-http vulnerable to SSRF via attacker-controlled OpenAPI servers[0].url in HTTP communication protocol
summary: The utcp-http plugin, version 1.1.1 and earlier, contains a blind SSRF flaw. register_manual() checks discovery URLs against an HTTPS or loopback allowlist, but call_tool() and call_tool_streaming() use the resolved tool_call_template.url without revalidating it, so an attacker-hosted OpenAPI spec can declare internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254 in servers[0].url. A prefix check also let http://localhost.evil.com bypass the loopback rule. The flaw affects the utcp_http.http, utcp_http.streamable_http and utcp_http.sse protocols and can expose cloud metadata and internal services to the LLM caller.
solution: Fixed in 1.1.2 (commit 5b16e43 on dev). The patch adds a utcp_http._security.ensure_secure_url() helper that validates hostnames by parsing, not string prefix, and calls it in register_manual() and before each aiohttp request in call_tool() and call_tool_streaming(). Workarounds: do not call register_manual() with URLs from untrusted parties, even over HTTPS, and restrict the agent host's outbound access to RFC1918, 169.254.0.0/16 and loopback addresses.

summary: AxonFlow's GHSA-9h64-2846-7x7f advisory consolidates eight bug fixes in the v7.1.3 to v7.5.0 window, closing multi-tenant isolation, access-control and policy-enforcement defects. title: GHSA-89vp-x53w-74fx: rmcp Streamable HTTP server transport has a DNS rebinding vulnerability
summary: Prior to version 1.4.0, the rmcp crate's Streamable HTTP server transport did not validate the incoming Host header, so a malicious public website using a DNS rebinding attack could send authenticated requests to a local or private-network MCP server. An attacker could enumerate and invoke exposed tools and read resources, and because MCP servers often run with the user's privileges, the impact can extend to arbitrary code execution on the victim's machine.
solution: Fixed in rmcp 1.4.0 (PR #764, commit 8e22aa2): StreamableHttpServerConfig::allowed_hosts now defaults to a loopback-only allowlist, and requests whose Host header is not on the allowlist receive HTTP 403. Upgrade to rmcp >= 1.4.0. If upgrade is not possible, place the MCP server behind a reverse proxy configured to reject requests whose Host header is not an expected hostname, and do not bind the server to 0.0.0.0 without such a proxy.

title: GHSA-83vm-p52w-f9pw: vLLM: extract_hidden_states speculative decoding crashes server on any request with penalty parameters
summary: A shape regression in vLLM's extract_hidden_states speculative decoding proposer, introduced when the KV connector interface was refactored in PR #37013, causes a RuntimeError that crashes the EngineCore process. title: GHSA-8cxw-cc62-q28v: ciguard: discover_pipeline_files follows symlinks out of scan root
summary: The discover_pipeline_files() function in src/ciguard/discovery.py, introduced in v0.8.0 and used by the MCP scan_repo tool in v0.8.1, follows symlinks during directory walks. An attacker who can plant a symlink in a scanned directory can make discovery return pipeline-shaped files outside the requested root, and an AI agent driven by an adversarial prompt can then read their content through later scan calls. The CVSS v3.1 score is 4.4 (Medium), and the v4.0 score is 5.7 (Medium) per the first.org calculator, while GitHub's calculator returns 2.4 (Low).
solution: Fixed in v0.8.2: discover_pipeline_files gains a follow_symlinks: bool = False parameter that refuses to descend into symlinked directories or files by default, and results are filtered to paths whose resolved location lies under the resolved root, even when follow_symlinks=True. A CI regression gate was added in v0.8.3.
affected_vendors_raw: ciguard MCP server; Claude Desktop; Claude Code; Cursor; Claude SDK for Python

summary: CVE-2026-42440 is an out-of-memory denial-of-service flaw in Apache OpenNLP's AbstractModelReader, affecting versions before 2.5.9 and before 3.0.0-M3. The methods getOutcomes(), getOutcomePatterns() and getPredicates() allocate arrays using an unvalidated 32-bit count read from a binary model stream. title: GHSA-56c3-vfp2-5qqj: n8n-mcp's IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses bypass SSRF protection in validateUrlSync(), enabling full SSRF for SDK embedders
summary: GHSA-56c3-vfp2-5qqj affects n8n-mcp deployments embedding the SDK via N8NDocumentationMCPServer or N8NMCPEngine with user-supplied InstanceContext, on versions v2.47.4 through v2.47.13. The synchronous validator SSRFProtection.validateUrlSync() had no IPv6 checks, so IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses such as http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254] bypassed cloud-metadata, localhost and private-IP checks. An attacker who controls n8nApiUrl can receive response bodies from internal targets, and the n8nApiKey is forwarded in the x-n8n-api-key header to the attacker-controlled host.
solution: Fixed in v2.47.14. Upgrade with `npx n8n-mcp@latest` (or pin to `>= 2.47.14`), or `docker pull ghcr.io/czlonkowski/n8n-mcp:latest`. Workarounds if upgrading is not immediate: reject n8nApiUrl values whose hostname is an IP literal (bracketed IPv6 or dotted IPv4) before calling the SDK; restrict egress from the process to RFC1918 ranges, 169.254.0.0/16 and cloud metadata endpoints; and do not accept user-controlled n8nApiUrl values.

title: GHSA-rch3-82jr-f9w9: Jupyter Notebook Vulnerable to Authentication Token Theft via CommandLinker XSS
summary: A stored XSS flaw in Jupyter Notebook lets attackers steal authentication tokens when users open malicious notebook files and click elements disguised as legitimate controls. solution: Jupyter Notebook 7.5.6 and JupyterLab 4.5.7 include patches for this vulnerability. The patched versions also allow disabling the command linker via `overrides.json` by setting `"@jupyterlab/apputils-extension:sanitizer": {"allowCommandLinker": false}`.

title: GHSA-p7fg-763f-g4gf: Claude SDK for TypeScript has Insecure Default File Permissions in Local Filesystem Memory Tool
summary: The Anthropic TypeScript SDK's `BetaLocalFilesystemMemoryTool` created memory files and directories with the Node.js default modes (`0o666` for files, `0o777` for directories). A local attacker on a shared host could read persisted agent state, and in containers could modify memory files to influence later model behavior.
solution: Users on the affected versions are advised to update to the latest version.

summary: The n8n dynamic-node-parameters endpoints did not check whether an authenticated caller was authorized to use a supplied credential reference. title: GHSA-f77h-j2v7-g6mw: n8n Vulnerable to Hijacking of Unauthenticated Chat Execution
summary: The `/chat` WebSocket endpoint used by n8n's Chat Trigger node did not verify that incoming connections were authorized for the target execution. An unauthenticated remote attacker who could identify a valid execution ID for a workflow in a waiting state could attach to that execution, receive the pending prompt meant for the legitimate user, and submit arbitrary input to resume or influence downstream workflow behavior. Exploitation requires a public Hosted Chat workflow with authentication set to `None`, a target execution in a waiting state, and knowledge of that execution ID.
solution: Fixed in n8n versions 1.123.32, 2.17.4, and 2.18.1; upgrade to one of these or later. Temporary workaround if upgrading is not immediately possible: set the Authentication field on all Chat Trigger nodes to `n8n User Auth` rather than `None`. The source states this workaround does not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as a short-term measure.

title: GHSA-f6x8-65q6-j9m9: n8n has Open Redirect in MCP OAuth Consent Flow
summary: n8n's `/mcp-oauth/register` endpoint accepts OAuth client registrations without authentication, so arbitrary `redirect_uri` values can be registered. When a user clicks Deny on the MCP OAuth consent dialog, the `handleDeny` handler redirects them to that registered URI without validation, creating an open redirect. title: GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g: Gemini CLI: Remote Code Execution via workspace trust and tool allowlisting bypasses
summary: Gemini CLI (`@google/gemini-cli`) and the `run-gemini-cli` GitHub Action are updated to harden workspace trust and tool allowlisting, especially in untrusted environments such as GitHub Actions. In headless mode, earlier versions automatically trusted workspace folders, so malicious environment variables in a local `.gemini/` directory could lead to remote code execution, and under `--yolo` the fine-grained tool allowlist in `~/.gemini/settings.json` was ignored. The update requires explicit folder trust and makes the policy engine evaluate tool allowlisting under `--yolo` (version `0.39.1`), which can break existing CI/CD workflows.
solution: The folder trust and tool allowlisting mitigations are available in `@google/gemini-cli` version `0.39.1` and `0.40.0-preview.3`. Users must review their workflows and take one of two approaches: 1. If the workflow runs on trusted inputs, set `GEMINI_TRUST_WORKSPACE: 'true'` in the workflow. 2. If the workflow runs on untrusted inputs, review the guidance in google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli to harden the workflow against malicious content, and set the environment variable. If the workflow specifies a version via `gemini_cli_version`, upgrade to one of the patched versions and audit the workflow settings that use Gemini CLI.

title: GHSA-r75f-5x8p-qvmc: LiteLLM has SQL Injection in Proxy API key verification
summary: LiteLLM's proxy API key verification mixed the caller-supplied key value into a database query instead of passing it as a separate parameter, enabling SQL injection. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted Authorization header to any LLM API route, such as POST /chat/completions, and reach the query through the proxy's error-handling path. The attacker can read proxy database data and may modify it, gaining unauthorised access to the proxy and the credentials it manages.

title: GHSA-2r2p-4cgf-hv7h: engram: HTTP server CORS wildcard + auth-off-by-default enables CSRF graph exfiltration and persistent indirect prompt injection
summary: The local HTTP server started by `engram server` (default `127.0.0.1:7337`) accepted requests from any browser origin with no authentication unless `ENGRAM_API_TOKEN` was set. Combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and a body parser that did not require `Content-Type: application/json`, a malicious web page could read the knowledge graph via `GET /query` and `GET /stats`, and write persistent prompt-injection payloads via `POST /learn`, which were later surfaced to the user's AI coding agent. Affected versions are `engramx` >= 1.0.0 and < 2.0.2.
solution: Fixed in `engramx@2.0.2`. Remediation in 2.0.2 includes fail-closed auth on non-public routes (Bearer header or HttpOnly cookie, constant-time comparison, 256-bit token at `~/.engram/http-server.token`), removal of wildcard CORS with an opt-in allowlist via `ENGRAM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, Host and Origin validation, enforced `Content-Type: application/json` on mutations, and a `/ui?token=` bootstrap with a `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate. Workarounds if upgrading is not possible: do not run `engram server` or `engram ui`, or set `ENGRAM_API_TOKEN` to a long random value and stop the server before browsing the web.

title: GHSA-r7w7-9xr2-qq2r: langchain-openai: Image token counting SSRF protection can be bypassed via DNS rebinding
summary: langchain-openai versions before 1.1.14 validated image URLs for SSRF protection in `_url_to_size()`, then fetched them with a separate DNS resolution, leaving a DNS rebinding window where a hostname could resolve to a public IP during validation and a private or localhost IP during the fetch. The fetched body is passed only to Pillow's `Image.open()` and never returned or logged, so an attacker cannot exfiltrate data, though blind probing of internal hosts and ports may be possible.
solution: Fixed in langchain-openai 1.1.14 (requires langchain-core >= 1.2.31). The fix replaces validate-then-fetch with `SSRFSafeSyncTransport` from langchain-core, which resolves DNS once, validates returned IPs against a policy, pins the connection to the validated IP, and disables redirect following.

title: GHSA-926x-3r5x-gfhw: LangChain has incomplete f-string validation in prompt templates
summary: LangChain's f-string prompt-template validation was incomplete in two ways. DictPromptTemplate and ImagePromptTemplate accepted templates with attribute access or indexing expressions and evaluated them during formatting, and validation did not reject nested replacement fields inside format specifiers. solution: LangChain now applies f-string safety validation consistently to DictPromptTemplate and ImagePromptTemplate, rejecting templates with attribute access or indexing during construction and deserialization. summary: GHSA-4ggg-h7ph-26qr describes an authenticated SSRF in n8n-mcp affecting versions up to and including 2.47.3. solution: Fixed in 2.1.48 (patched version: @lobehub/lobehub 2.1.48). The source also suggests requiring a server-validated session, OIDC token or validated API key for protected webapi routes, removing the apiKey truthiness check as an auth decision, and signing any client payload server-side with an HMAC or replacing it with a session-bound backend lookup.

title: GHSA-69x8-hrgq-fjj8: LiteLLM: Password hash exposure and pass-the-hash authentication bypass
summary: LiteLLM stores user passwords as unsalted SHA-256 hashes and returns the password hash field from /user/info, /user/update and /spend/users to any authenticated user regardless of role. The /v2/login endpoint accepts the raw SHA-256 hash as a valid password, so an authenticated user can retrieve another user's hash and log in as that user, escalating privileges in three HTTP requests.
solution: Fixed in v1.83.0. Passwords are now hashed with scrypt (random 16-byte salt, n=16384, r=8, p=1), password hashes are stripped from all API responses, and existing SHA-256 hashes are transparently migrated on next login.

title: GHSA-44c2-3rw4-5gvh: PraisonAI Has SSRF in FileTools.download_file() via Unvalidated URL
summary: GHSA-44c2-3rw4-5gvh reports an SSRF flaw in FileTools.download_file() in praisonaiagents. The function checks the destination path but passes the caller-supplied url directly to httpx.stream() with follow_redirects=True, so an attacker who controls the URL can reach any host the server can access, including cloud metadata services and internal services. On EC2 instances with IMDSv1 enabled, IAM credentials can be retrieved and written to disk, and the flaw is reachable through indirect prompt injection without authentication.
solution: Suggested fix: validate the url before the request by allowing only the http and https schemes and blocking loopback, link-local (169.254.0.0/16), and private RFC 1918 address ranges, as shown in the source's _validate_url() example.

title: GHSA-r4f2-3m54-pp7q: PraisonAI Has Sandbox Escape via shell=True and Bypassable Blocklist in SubprocessSandbox
summary: In PraisonAI, `SubprocessSandbox` runs commands through `subprocess.run()` with `shell=True` and blocks dangerous commands only by string-pattern matching. The blocklist omits `sh` and `bash`, so in STRICT mode a call such as `sh -c 'id'` escapes the sandbox, and blocked commands like curl, wget, nc and ssh become reachable. Combined with agent prompt injection, an attacker could reach the network, filesystem and cloud metadata services. The source reports testing on praisonai==4.5.87.
solution: The source suggests replacing `shell=True` with `shell=False` and passing `shlex.split(command)` to `subprocess.run()`. It does not state a fixed version.

title: GHSA-xrf2-5r3p-5wgj: libcrux: Panic in Signature Hint Decoding During Verification
summary: The libcrux-ml-dsa library's hint decoding during ML-DSA signature verification did not check the boundedness of the cumulative hint counter for the last row of the hint vector. title: GHSA-jfjg-vc52-wqvf: BentoML has Dockerfile Command Injection via system_packages in bentofile.yaml
summary: BentoML's docker.system_packages field in bentofile.yaml accepts arbitrary strings that are interpolated unescaped into Dockerfile RUN commands. title: GHSA-m63j-689w-3j35: n8n is Vulnerable to Credential Theft via Name-Based Resolution and Permission Checker Bypass in Community Edition
summary: An authenticated user with the global:member role can chain flaws in n8n's credential pipeline to steal plaintext secrets from generic HTTP credentials (httpBasicAuth, httpHeaderAuth, httpQueryAuth) owned by other users on the same instance. title: GHSA-xq7h-vwjp-5vrh: @grackle-ai/powerline Runs Without Authentication by Default
summary: The PowerLine gRPC server in @grackle-ai/powerline runs with no authentication when neither the --token flag nor the GRACKLE_POWERLINE_TOKEN variable is set. title: GHSA-647h-p824-99w7: @grackle-ai/mcp has a workspace authorization bypass in its knowledge_search MCP tool
summary: The knowledge_search and knowledge_get_node MCP tools in @grackle-ai/mcp are listed in SCOPED_TOOLS, so scoped agents can call them, but their handlers do not receive authContext or enforce workspace scoping. A scoped agent in Workspace A can pass an arbitrary workspaceId to read knowledge graph data from Workspace B, bypassing workspace isolation (CWE-284).
solution: Fix: Add an authContext parameter to the knowledge_search and knowledge_get_node handlers and enforce workspace scoping, matching knowledge_create_node, using resolvedWorkspaceId = authContext?.type === "scoped" ? authContext.workspaceId ?? "" : workspaceId ?? "". Workarounds: do not use scoped agent tokens in multi-workspace deployments until patched, or remove knowledge_search and knowledge_get_node from the SCOPED_TOOLS set in tool-scoping.ts.

title: GHSA-7q9x-8g6p-3x75: @grackle-ai/server: Unescaped Error String in renderPairingPage() HTML Template
summary: GHSA-7q9x-8g6p-3x75 affects @grackle-ai/server. Its renderPairingPage() function interpolates the error parameter into HTML without escaping, unlike renderAuthorizePage() in the same file, which uses escapeHtml(). solution:

${escapeHtml(error)}

` : "";

summary: An authenticated user with permission to create or modify workflows can use the JavaScript Task Runner in n8n to allocate uninitialized memory buffers. Excel sheet names are concatenated into PostgreSQL table names and embedded in COPY statements via f-strings, so any authenticated user, even the lowest-privileged, can reach remote code execution through a two-stage upload that bypasses the 31-character sheet name limit. Confirmed impacts include command execution as the postgres user, exfiltration of files such as /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, and full database takeover.

title: GHSA-g2j9-7rj2-gm6c: Langflow has an Arbitrary File Write (RCE) via v2 API
summary: GHSA-g2j9-7rj2-gm6c reports an Arbitrary File Write in Langflow via the POST /api/v2/files/ endpoint. The multipart upload filename is passed unchecked to LocalStorageService, which lacks a containment check, so an authenticated attacker can write files anywhere on the host, potentially leading to Remote Code Execution. The reporter tested this against langflowai/langflow:latest (v1.7.3).
solution: Sanitize the multipart filename before processing by stripping directory components with pathlib's name attribute and rejecting empty names or names containing ".." with HTTP 400. Also add a canonical path containment check inside LocalStorageService.save_file.

title: GHSA-89xv-2j6f-qhc8: Cross-Site Tool Execution for HTTP Servers without Authorizatrion in github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk
summary: The Go SDK for MCP (github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk) had a flaw in its Streamable HTTP transport. It accepted browser-generated cross-site POST requests without validating the Origin header or requiring Content-Type: application/json. Without Authorization configured, especially in stateless or sessionless setups, any website could send MCP requests to a local server and potentially trigger tool execution. Cross-site POSTs with Content-Type: text/plain could reach message handling without a CORS preflight barrier.
solution: Fixed in v1.4.1, which adds Content-Type header validation for POST requests and a configurable origin verification protection (commit a433a83). Note: v1.4.1 requires Go 1.25 or later.

title: GHSA-q382-vc8q-7jhj: Improper handling of null Unicode character when parsing JSON in github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk
summary: The Go SDK for the Model Context Protocol moved to the segmentio/encoding library for JSON parsing in version 1.3.1. The new parser matched keys that had null Unicode characters appended to their base names, so combined with duplicate keys, a "last key wins" resolution could override the intended MCP message. This could let messages evade proxies or policy layers that match exact field names, and other MCP SDKs in TypeScript and Python would reject the same messages.
solution: The segmentio/encoding package was patched and released as v0.5.4, and the SDK switched to the patched dependency in 724dd47aa. Users are advised to update to v1.4.1.

title: GHSA-mmgp-wc2j-qcv7: Claude Code has a Workspace Trust Dialog Bypass via Repo-Controlled Settings File

title: GHSA-3xm7-qw7j-qc8v: SSRF in @aborruso/ckan-mcp-server via base_url allows access to internal networks
summary: The @aborruso/ckan-mcp-server MCP server accepts a base_url parameter in tools such as ckan_package_search and sparql_query and sends HTTP requests to it without restriction. Exploitation needs prompt injection through malicious content while the assistant has this server connected, and a proof of concept sent 9 requests to a canary endpoint. An attacker could scan internal networks, steal cloud metadata credentials via 169.254.169.254, and attempt SQL or SPARQL injection.
solution: Recommended fix: 1. Validate base_url against a configurable allowlist of permitted CKAN portals. 2. Block private IP ranges (RFC 1918, link-local). 3. Block cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254). 4. Sanitize SQL input for datastore queries. 5. Apply a SPARQL endpoint allowlist.

title: GHSA-rf6x-r45m-xv3w: Langflow is Missing Ownership Verification in API Key Deletion (IDOR)
summary: Langflow's DELETE endpoint for API keys, delete_api_key_route() in src/backend/base/langflow/api/v1/api_key.py, checks only that the caller is authenticated. The delete_api_key() CRUD function in crud.py does not verify that the key belongs to the current user, so any authenticated user can delete other users' API keys by ID. The source says this enables account takeover, denial of service, and disruption of other users' integrations.
solution: Pass current_user to the delete function; in delete_api_key(), verify api_key.user_id == current_user.id before deletion; raise a 403 Forbidden error if the user does not own the key. Example: if api_key.user_id != user_id: raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail='Unauthorized')

title: GHSA-5h2m-4q8j-pqpj: FastMCP OAuth Proxy token reuse across MCP servers
summary: The FastMCP OAuth Proxy ignores the client-supplied `resource` parameter in authorization and token requests and issues tokens for the `base_url` set at initialization instead. Because the tokens carry no resource information, a benign MCP server cannot verify that a token was issued for it. An attacker can run a malicious MCP server that advertises the benign proxy as its authorization server, capture the token from a victim's OAuth flow, and replay it against other MCP servers that share that authorization server.
solution: To mitigate this vulnerability, it is recommended to issue tokens specifically for the MCP server submitted in the authorization URL's `resource` GET parameter. In this way, the receiving MCP server will be able to properly verify that the token was indeed issued for it, allowing it to reject tokens stolen by an attack like the one demonstrated above.

The issue is rated CVSS 3.1 8.6 (High) under CWE-306.

title: GHSA-cwc3-p92j-g7qm: Flowise has IDOR leading to Account Takeover and Enterprise Feature Bypass via SSO Configuration
summary: GHSA-cwc3-p92j-g7qm describes an Insecure Direct Object Reference in the PUT /api/v1/loginmethod endpoint of the Flowise platform. The endpoint accepts an organizationId from the JSON body and updates that organization's record without checking that the authenticated user owns it or has admin rights, so any low-privileged user, including Free plan users, can overwrite another organization's SSO configuration. The source states this enables Account Takeover by replacing the victim's OAuth credentials with attacker-controlled ones, and enabling Enterprise-only SSO features without a license.
solution: N/A -- no mitigation discussed in source.

title: GHSA-mq4r-h2gh-qv7x: Flowise Allows Mass Assignment in `/api/v1/leads` Endpoint
summary: A mass assignment flaw in the `/api/v1/leads` endpoint of Flowise lets unauthenticated users set internal entity fields (`id`, `createdDate`, `chatId`) by including them in the request body. The `createLead` function in `/packages/server/src/services/leads/index.ts` calls `Object.assign(newLead, body)` without filtering fields, overwriting the auto-generated values before save. The endpoint is listed in `WHITELIST_URLS` in `/packages/server/src/utils/constants.ts`, so no authentication is required. The source is tagged CWE-915.
solution: N/A -- no mitigation discussed in source.

title: GHSA-j8g8-j7fc-43v6: Flowise has Arbitrary File Upload via MIME Spoofing
summary: The `/api/v1/attachments/:chatflowId/:chatId` endpoint in Flowise is listed in `WHITELIST_URLS`, so it accepts uploads without authentication. The server checks uploads against the MIME types in `chatbotConfig.fullFileUpload.allowedUploadFileTypes` but trusts the client-supplied `Content-Type` header without checking file contents or extension. An attacker can upload scripts or other arbitrary files by declaring a permitted type such as `application/pdf`, and the files persist in backend storage. Chained with static hosting or file retrieval, this can lead to Stored XSS, malicious file hosting, or Remote Code Execution.
solution: N/A -- no mitigation discussed in source.

title: GHSA-wvhq-wp8g-c7vq: Flowise has Authorization Bypass via Spoofed x-request-from Header
summary: Flowise trusts any HTTP client that sends the header `x-request-from: internal`, so an authenticated tenant session with only a browser cookie can bypass the authorization checks on `/api/v1/**`. The flaw sits in the global middleware at `external/Flowise/packages/server/src/index.ts:214`, which calls `verifyToken` for that header and runs no further permission checks. The source says the bypass grants access to internal administration endpoints such as `/api/v1/apikey`, `/api/v1/credentials`, `/api/v1/tools` and `/api/v1/node-custom-function`, and that all self-hosted Flowise 3.0.8 deployments using the default middleware are affected.
solution: N/A -- no mitigation discussed in source.

title: GHSA-g8r9-g2v8-jv6f: GitHub Copilot CLI Dangerous Shell Expansion Patterns Enable Arbitrary Code Execution
summary: GitHub Copilot CLI's shell tool contains a vulnerability in which crafted bash parameter expansion patterns (such as ${var@P}, assignment forms like ${var=value}, indirect ${!var}, and nested $(cmd) inside ${...}) can hide command execution inside commands the safety assessment classifies as read-only. An attacker who can influence the commands the agent runs, for example through prompt injection in repository files, MCP server responses, or user instructions, could achieve arbitrary code execution on the user's workstation, even in modes that require approval for write operations. The issue affects versions prior to 0.0.423.
solution: Fixed in 0.0.423. The fix adds parse-time detection that downgrades commands containing dangerous ${...} expansion operators or nested command/process substitutions from read-only to write-capable, and unconditionally blocks such commands at the tool execution layer regardless of permission mode, including --yolo / autopilot.

title: GHSA-jc5m-wrp2-qq38: Flowise Vulnerable to PII Disclosure on Unauthenticated Forgot Password Endpoint
summary: Flowise's POST /api/v1/account/forgot-password endpoint returns the full user object, including id, name, email, status and timestamps, instead of a generic acknowledgment. title: GHSA-x2g5-fvc2-gqvp: Flowise has Insufficient Password Salt Rounds
summary: Flowise's getHash function in packages/server/src/enterprise/utils/encryption.util.ts uses a default bcrypt salt round count of 5, set through the PASSWORD_SALT_HASH_ROUNDS environment variable, which yields 2^5 = 32 iterations. The source states this is below the OWASP recommendation of 10 rounds (1024 iterations), so stored password hashes are easier to brute-force if the database is compromised. The same default is used in resetPassword (account.service.ts:568). Tracked as CWE-916 with Medium severity.
solution: Increase default PASSWORD_SALT_HASH_ROUNDS to at least 10 (recommended by OWASP). Consider using 12 for better security-performance balance. Document that higher values increase login time but improve security.

title: GHSA-g48c-2wqr-h844: LangGraph checkpoint loading has unsafe msgpack deserialization
summary: LangGraph checkpointers can load msgpack-encoded checkpoints that reconstruct Python objects during deserialization. An attacker who can write attacker-controlled checkpoint bytes to the backing store, for example after a database compromise, may supply a crafted payload that triggers unsafe object reconstruction when the checkpoint is loaded, potentially leading to code execution in the application runtime. The source states there is no evidence of exploitation in the wild.
solution: LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK: when set to a truthy value (1, true, yes), the default msgpack deserialization policy becomes strict, so JsonPlusSerializer() defaults allowed_msgpack_modules to None instead of True unless allowed_msgpack_modules is explicitly passed. Set allowed_msgpack_modules to None for strict mode, which reconstructs only a built-in safe set, or to a list of (module, class_name) tuples to allow exactly the listed symbols in addition to that set. When strict mode is enabled and a StateGraph is compiled, LangGraph derives an allowlist from the graph's schemas and channels and applies it to the checkpointer.

title: GHSA-5hwf-rc88-82xm: Fickling missing RCE-capable modules in UNSAFE_IMPORTS
summary: fickling versions up to and including 0.1.8 have an incomplete UNSAFE_IMPORTS blocklist that omits the stdlib modules uuid, _osx_support and _aix_support. Functions in these modules, such as uuid._get_command_stdout, _aix_support._read_cmd_output and _osx_support._find_build_tool, call subprocess.Popen() or os.system() with attacker-controlled arguments. A malicious pickle importing them passes fickling's UnsafeImports and NonStandardImports checks, and pickle.loads() runs the command.
solution: Assessment: the modules uuid, _osx_support and _aix_support were added to the blocklist of unsafe imports (https://github.com/trailofbits/fickling/commit/ffac3479dbb97a7a1592d85991888562d34dd05b).

title: GHSA-9mph-4f7v-fmvh: OpenClaw has agent avatar symlink traversal in gateway session metadata
summary: A crafted local avatar path in OpenClaw's gateway can follow a symlink outside the agent workspace and return arbitrary file contents as a base64 data: URL. The flaw sits in resolveIdentityAvatarUrl in src/gateway/session-utils.ts, affects the openclaw npm package from v2026.1.21 through 2026.2.21-2, and allows local file read in the gateway process, which agents.list can return as avatarUrl.
solution: Resolve workspace and avatar paths with realpath and enforce realpath containment. Open files with O_NOFOLLOW when available. Compare pre-open and opened file identity (dev/ino) to block swap races. Add regression tests for outside-workspace symlink rejection and in-workspace symlink allowance. Planned patched version: 2026.2.22.

title: GHSA-659f-22xc-98f2: OpenClaw hook transform path containment missed symlink-resolved escapes
summary: The openclaw npm package, versions up to and including 2026.2.21-2, validated webhook transform modules with lexical path checks only. title: GHSA-943q-mwmv-hhvh: OpenClaw: Gateway /tools/invoke tool escalation + ACP permission auto-approval
summary: OpenClaw Gateway's authenticated POST /tools/invoke endpoint did not deny high-risk session orchestration tools such as sessions_spawn and sessions_send by default, so a caller holding a valid Gateway token could create or control agent sessions and inject messages across sessions. ACP clients could also auto-approve permission requests for risky tools with insufficient user interaction. The advisory rates it CVSS 8.8 and affects openclaw versions before 2026.2.14.
solution: Fixed in openclaw >= 2026.2.14. Deployment guidance: keep the Gateway loopback-only (gateway.bind="loopback" or openclaw gateway run --bind loopback), avoid direct public internet exposure and use an SSH tunnel or Tailscale instead, and audit any configuration that opts into default-denied HTTP tools via gateway.tools.allow.

title: GHSA-wvj2-96wp-fq3f: MCP Go SDK Vulnerable to Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
summary: The Go MCP SDK parsed JSON-RPC and MCP messages with Go's standard encoding/json.Unmarshal, which matches keys case-insensitively and folds Unicode characters such as ſ (U+017F) and K (U+212A) to ASCII. A malicious MCP peer could send non-standard field casing, such as "Method" instead of "method", that the SDK silently accepted. This could let such messages bypass intermediary proxies or policy layers that match exact field names, and it made the Go SDK inconsistent with the case-sensitive TypeScript and Python SDKs.
solution: Fixed in v1.3.1. The SDK replaced Go's standard JSON unmarshaling with a case-sensitive decoder (github.com/segmentio/encoding) in commit 7b8d81c. Users are advised to update to v1.3.1.

title: GHSA-76rv-2r9v-c5m6: zae-limiter: DynamoDB hot partition throttling enables per-entity Denial of Service
summary: The zae-limiter library places all rate limit buckets for one entity under a single DynamoDB partition key (`namespace/ENTITY#{id}`). A high-traffic entity can exceed DynamoDB's per-partition throughput limit of about 1,000 WCU/sec, causing `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` throttling that degrades that entity and possibly other entities sharing the partition. The source states that no built-in mitigation exists in the library at present.
solution: The source proposes a remediation design called Pre-Shard Buckets: buckets move to `PK={ns}/BUCKET#{entity}#{resource}#{shard}, SK=#STATE` so each (entity, resource, shard) gets its own partition, shards double from 1 to 2 to 4 to 8 on `wcu` exhaustion or proactively by the aggregator, and an auto-injected `wcu:1000` reserved limit tracks partition write pressure. The source describes this as a design, not a released fix, and names no fixed version.

Stateless deployments without sessionIdGenerator are most exposed, and the two issues may affect a deployment separately or together.

title: GHSA-x34r-63hx-w57f: Langroid has WAF Bypass Leading to RCE in TableChatAgent
summary: Langroid versions up to and including 0.59.31 are affected by a bypass of the WAF in `langroid/utils/pandas_utils.py` that was added for CVE-2025-46724. The source reports this allows arbitrary shell command execution on the server.

title: CVE-2025-61784: LLaMA-Factory is a tuning library for large language models. Prior to version 0.9.4, a Server-Side Request Forgery…
summary: CVE-2025-61784 affects LLaMA-Factory before version 0.9.4. An authenticated user can abuse a Server-Side Request Forgery flaw in the chat API to make the server send arbitrary HTTP requests to internal and external networks, exposing internal services and enabling network reconnaissance. The flaw lies in the `_process_request` function in `src/llamafactory/api/chat.py`, which calls `requests.get(url, stream=True).raw` on multimodal URLs without validating them.
solution: Fixed in 0.9.4.

solution: A server-side patch stopped streaming back newlines or control characters, released September 27, 2024. The server-side patch applies to older versions of Cursor, so no additional action is needed for it. Cursor's maintainers also recommend including only trusted pieces of context in prompts.

title: CVE-2020-15201: In Tensorflow before version 2.3.1, the `RaggedCountSparseOutput` implementation does not validate that the input…
summary: TensorFlow versions before 2.3.1 contain a flaw in the `RaggedCountSparseOutput` implementation, which does not validate that its input arguments form a valid ragged tensor. solution: Patched in commit 3cbb917b4714766030b28eba9fb41bb97ce9ee02 and released in TensorFlow version 2.3.1.
